question: Should OpenClaw adopt RFC 0018’s opt-in canonical readiness contract, including gateway.readiness activation, required/advisory conditions, subject identity, and activation-scoped plugin providers?
rationale: These choices establish new operator configuration and plugin-facing behavior; source review cannot determine the intended permanent product contract.

options.title: Sponsor the RFC direction
options.body: Open a maintainer discussion, confirm the four contract decisions, and have the RFC link the resulting decision before merge.

options.title: Narrow the first version
options.body: Accept only the legacy-compatible canonical core condition model and defer plugin providers or subject identity until their API ownership is separately agreed.

options.title: Pause the proposal
options.body: Leave the RFC unmerged until an owner is available to define readiness as an endorsed product surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the RFC direction
recommendation.body: Open a maintainer discussion, confirm the four contract decisions, and have the RFC link the resulting decision before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the active proposal steward and recent contributor to merged RFC work, so they are the best available coordinator for bringing the decision to the appropriate maintainers.
